A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MSB benchmark. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated appendices and retained attack examples.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of nine LLM agents, with attack success and task-performance results in Table 3, Figures 2–3 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these results and adds GPT-5 evaluations, MCIP defense results in Table 4, and a Qwen3 thinking-mode experiment in Table 13.

M1.justification: The proposed attack-construction procedures, MCP execution framework and NRP formula remain unchanged. Expanded construction explanations document existing procedures; MCIP is an evaluated external defense, not a new proposed method component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain 10 domains, 65 user tasks, six attack goals, 304 benign tools and 2,000 attack instances. Specifying 405 attack tools instead of '400+' clarifies the count without establishing changed coverage. The added experiments use the existing benchmark.

E2.justification: GPT-5 joins the nine retained model backbones in the reported comparisons. Section 6.3 additionally evaluates MCIP against agents without defense; v1 cited MCIP but did not evaluate it. The benchmark feature comparison in Table 10 is descriptive, not a new performance evaluation.

E3.justification: v2 adds defense-versus-no-defense evaluation across ten backbones and a Qwen3 8B thinking-on/off comparison controlling model size, architecture and alignment. Existing benchmark metrics and core evaluation settings are retained. Newly explained filtering and success-check procedures do not establish changes to earlier experiments.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands supplementary investigation through MCIP defense testing, a controlled thinking-mode ablation addressing the utility–security relationship, and task/tool performance distributions in Figure 4. The original stage/tool-configuration analyses and illustrated attack cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new task/tool histograms describe performance heterogeneity, not uncertainty across repeated experiments; averaging over an additional model does not change uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: The original nine models' tabulated results are unchanged. GPT-5 adds a 37.17% average ASR, changing the across-model average from 40.71% to 40.35%. New Table 4 reports MCIP reducing average ASR from 40.35% to 28.69% while reducing PUA from 56.50% to 48.91%. Table 13 adds thinking-mode results with higher PUA and ASR; Appendix D adds task/tool distribution findings.

T1.justification: The threat assumptions, mathematical objectives and metric definitions retain their substantive meaning. Simplified equation notation and the new Appendix B/Table 5 explain and summarize existing formalism. No new theorem, proof or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: v2 removes the claim that MSB is the 'first' such benchmark from the abstract, introduction, contributions and conclusion. The central contributions and claims about MCP vulnerability and the utility–security relationship remain; the reported evaluation scope increases from nine to ten models.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 corrects v1's reversed explanation of higher versus lower NRP. Section 6.3 adds substantive defense limitations involving over-rejection, failed tool calls and attacks hidden until execution. Appendix E expands interpretations of parameter deception, mixed-attack synergy and thinking-related vulnerability, while retaining the broader utility–security interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility documentation with tool-filtering and deduplication criteria, per-domain task counts, attack-instance composition, attack-type distributions and explicit success checks in Table 9. The abstract also adds a code-repository link. These are newly documented details and access information, not evidence that the original benchmark was rebuilt.

R1.justification: Appendix D.5/Table 10 makes comparisons with the already cited MCPTox, ASB, AgentDojo and InjecAgent more explicit. v2 adds the GPT-5 system-card reference, removes Liu et al.'s multimodal-jailbreak survey, and narrows the priority claim. The main research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in Section 5.1, attack explanations and results discussion. The construction appendix is reorganized, a notation appendix is inserted, and conference headers and acknowledgments are added. Most of the original narrative and attack-example prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: New defense, thinking-mode, notation and benchmark-comparison tables substantially expand the displays, alongside task/tool histograms and an instance-distribution chart. Figures 2–3 are redrawn to include GPT-5, and construction tables gain explanatory columns. The original attack-example images and system-prompt image are retained.

improvement.justification: Correcting the reversed NRP explanation and documenting success checks improve correctness and transparency. The defense comparison and thinking-mode control add useful evidence about security–utility trade-offs. These gains remain bounded: the added investigations cover one defense and one model's thinking toggle, lack uncertainty reporting, and do not establish the broadly stated inverse-scaling claim.
